question: Does every declared record identifier in ledger/citation_audit.csv resolve to a bibliographic record that is the work the row declares (title/authors/year), and do the two identifiers of a row that carries both a DOI and an arXiv id resolve to the same work?
why_now: G-LIT requires resolvable locators and independent re-fetch spot checks. Existing independent coverage is 7/97 rows (worker-099 check #4: 6 MATCH / 1 FAIL) plus earlier partial sample checks. No full-population identity check exists; 59 rows carry both a DOI and an arXiv id and were never cross-checked against each other.

sampling_rule.rule: census, not sample: every row of the frozen CSV and every distinct non-empty doi / arxiv_id value is queried. No row is dropped after fetch.

method.doi: one GET https://api.crossref.org/works/<doi> per unique DOI, User-Agent with mailto; record HTTP status and message.title / message.author / message.issued
method.arxiv: batched GET https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=<ids> in chunks of <=50; parse Atom entries; record title, authors, published year, and any declared doi
method.comparison: title normalization (case-fold, LaTeX/brace strip, accent fold, token sort) then both token-set Jaccard and difflib ratio; a row is IDENTITY_MATCH when the DOI-resolved and arXiv-resolved records are title-compatible at thresholds fixed below, or when Crossref/arXiv metadata themselves carry a cross-identifier (arXiv id in Crossref, DOI in arXiv) linking them
method.declared_title_check: each resolved title is also compared to the row's declared title with the same thresholds

thresholds_frozen_at_preregistration.note: Fixed before any fetch. A pair counts as compatible if jaccard >= 0.6 OR ratio >= 0.8. Both metrics are reported per row so a reader can re-judge at any threshold.

verdict_vocabulary.IDENTITY_MATCH: both identifier channels resolve to title-compatible records
verdict_vocabulary.IDENTITY_MISMATCH: the two identifier channels resolve to title-incompatible records
verdict_vocabulary.DOI_TITLE_MISMATCH: the DOI resolves to a record whose title is incompatible with the row's declared title
verdict_vocabulary.ARXIV_TITLE_MISMATCH: the arXiv id resolves to a record whose title is incompatible with the row's declared title
verdict_vocabulary.FETCH_FAILED: an identifier could not be resolved (HTTP non-200 after retries); reported, never silently dropped
verdict_vocabulary.NO_IDENTIFIER: row carries neither a DOI nor an arXiv id (INSPIRE record only)

falsifiers: Re-running run_identity_audit_025.py --offline on the shipped cache does not regenerate report.json at the same sha256.
Any row reported IDENTITY_MATCH is shown, from the cached API bodies, to have resolved to two different works.
Any row reported IDENTITY_MISMATCH has a cached DOI record and cached arXiv record that are title-compatible at the frozen thresholds.
A declared identifier resolves to a record whose authors or year contradict the row's declared authors/year (reportable as a separate mismatch class, measured in the same pass).
known_risks: Crossref titles for a published version can differ in subtitle/punctuation from the arXiv preprint title; thresholds and per-row metrics are reported so this is visible rather than hidden in a verdict.
Publisher bot-blocking (HTTP 403) is not evidence of an invalid identifier; such rows are reported FETCH_FAILED and routed as unresolved, not as mismatches.
Absence of a mismatch is not acceptance of the ledger; this task does not set a gate or node verdict.
non_claims: Does not claim the evidence excerpts support the theorems (worker-099 SRC-025 FAIL and the L0 content verdicts own that question).
Does not edit the ledger, the map, or any frozen artifact.
Does not promote validation_status or any gate verdict.
expected_information_gain: Completes population-level identifier identity coverage for L1 from 7/97 to 97/97 rows, and tests the 59 dual-identifier rows against each other for the first time.
